name: Ipamorelin

lead: Ipamorelin is a synthetic pentapeptide that selectively stimulates growth hormone release. Novo Nordisk developed it in the 1990s, and it is now sold as a research peptide.
Clinical work has been limited, mainly early pharmacology and a trial in post-surgical bowel recovery that showed no clear benefit. Claims for muscle and fat loss are unsupported by good human data.

paras: It is a selective agonist of the ghrelin receptor (GHS-R1a), triggering pulsatile pituitary growth hormone release with relatively little effect on cortisol and prolactin compared with older secretagogues.

It is not approved for human use and is banned in sport. Short-term data are limited; theoretical concerns include insulin resistance, fluid retention and effects of long-term GH/IGF-1 elevation. Product quality is unregulated.
